title: Parents Report Losing Sleep to 'Techxiety'
paragraphs: Many parents lie awake at night worrying about their children. According to a new survey, technology is now one of the biggest reasons, and some people are calling this "techxiety."

The survey was carried out online by Talker Research in May 2026. It asked 2,000 American parents of school-aged children about their worries. The survey was paid for by Cosmo, a company that sells smartwatches for children.

According to the survey, parents lose an average of seven hours of sleep every week because they are worried about their children. This is equal to about 48 nights a year. Technology is the biggest cause. The top worries at night were screen time habits, at 24%, the effect of social media on children's self-esteem, at 20%, and addiction to games or apps, at 18%.

Parents whose children have smartphones lose nearly two more hours of sleep each week than other parents. They are also more likely to worry about their child's mental health, at 31% compared with 27%.
The survey found that 73% of parents said their child already had a smartphone. Some parents see this as a "loss of innocence," at 38%, while 62% see it as a step toward independence.

Phones at school are another concern. Many US states have introduced rules that limit phones in schools. However, nine in 10 parents in the survey want their children to have phone access at school, and 60% of those parents said it should only be for emergencies.

In addition, 77% of parents said they would like a device that keeps them connected with their child but limits distractions. Russell York, the head of Cosmo, said that staying connected with a child "shouldn't require handing them the entire internet."
However, because the survey was paid for by a company that sells devices for children, its results should be read with some care.
